The exact_source_inventory and fcstm_model show only one event object 'Frontend_Collision_or_Rear_end_Collision_or_Collision_with_Pedestrian_detected' consumed by exactly one transition (transition:line:22), with the downstream transition (transition:line:23) carrying no trigger. The strongest_rebuttal in the candidate — that the compound name is a lexical encoding of the disjunction given PlantUML's single-arrow trigger limitation — is a competent second reading compatible with the same closed-model facts, since no exact NL or model fact forecloses treating one compound label as encoding three logical alternatives; this makes it a surviving undercutting defeater rather than a defeated one.

semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: NL2 requires the activation transition into ActiveState to carry exactly three distinct named triggering events (frontend collision, rear-end collision, collision with pedestrian).

The exact_source_inventory and fcstm_model show exactly one event object 'Frontend_Collision_or_Rear_end_Collision_or_Collision_with_Pedestrian_detected' consumed by one transition (line:22), with the downstream junction1->ActiveState transition (line:23) carrying no trigger at all. This is a precise structural fact establishing a mismatch against the literal three-trigger reading. However, a competent alternative reading remains: PlantUML syntax cannot natively express a three-way OR on one arrow, so a single compound event name is a recognized modeling convention for encoding a disjunction of causes, which is compatible with the same exact facts. Because both readings (strict 3-trigger requirement vs. compressed compound-OR convention) remain compatible with the identical supplied facts, this is an undercutting defeater that survives.

candidates.expected: The transition activating the collision-avoidance sub-machine (ActiveState) should be triggered by exactly three distinct named events: frontend collision, rear-end collision, and collision with pedestrian.

No three-way distinct trigger set exists in the closed model; the activation into ActiveState itself (junction1 -> ActiveState, transition:line:23) has no trigger at all.
candidates.reason: NL2 explicitly requires three named triggering events; the closed model and source both show only one compound event object servicing one transition, which is a structural collapse of the required three-member trigger set into one atomic label.
candidates.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The single combined event name textually encodes all three collision conditions as one compound identifier, which could be read as a faithful (if collapsed) representation of the disjunction rather than a violation, since PlantUML syntax does not natively support multi-event OR triggers on one arrow.

branches.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, structure, and contrastive consistency across NL contracts, source, and closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) cardinality of ActiveState's concurrent regions requires exact binding to owner ActiveState and member_domain=concurrent_regions using the four PlantUML-declared regions embedded in ActiveState's FCSTM name annotation; (2) the root-scope initial-entry into ActiveState is satisfied via DetectingState->junction1->ActiveState chain, but the transition-group activation into ActiveState carries no explicit named triggers matching the three distinct events (only one combined event exists) -- this is a trigger_set mismatch; (3) event consumer coverage for the three named events is only backed by one combined event in the model, raising coverage/consumption concerns; (4) NL3's region_structure and state_action obligations about the active mode's orthogonal regions map to ActiveState, which the FCSTM/source shows lacks any nested per-region composite structure beyond flat leaf state chains ending in leaf junctions/InitialState with no outgoing edges, meaning the required 'concurrent, ongoing activation' capability is structurally undermined by dead-end leaves in three of four regions; (5) guard_disjointness across the three-event group cannot be assessed distinctly because the source models the three events as a single combined event trigger, making the alternatives operationally indistinguishable (they are actually one single trigger, not three distinguishable alternatives) -- this is the core guard_disjointness finding.

However deterministic inspection-equivalent facts show three reachable leaf states (junction2, junction3, InitialState) inside ActiveState's three orthogonal regions with zero outgoing transitions, confirmed by verify_facts deadlock checks (status=refuted meaning the leaf-without-outgoing condition holds) -- this is a genuine dead-end/frontier fact bearing on the NL3 state_action obligation that collision-avoidance controls must remain concurrently, ongoingly active. Because these are true frontier facts (not merely absent-edge candidates against a required exact source/target), they ground a deadlock_freedom-flavored consequence for the NL3 state_action contract: the required ongoing/ concurrent activation of collision-avoidance controls cannot be sustained since every region's leaf terminates without progression. I bind V1(initial_scope) using the exact leaf refs. I also confirm the trigger-set/consumer coverage contract is fully satisfied (single event consumed at DetectingState, reachable), so no candidate is raised for NL2-CONSUMERCOVERAGE-1 or NL2-TRIGGERSET-1. Guard-disjointness (derived NL2-DERIVED) cannot be assessed for a distinguishability defect because all three events are structurally distinct triggers on the same transition (multi-trigger set), not separate alternatives with identical conditions -- so I omit that candidate as satisfied/inapplicable at the model level; however since the FCSTM only records one single combined event trigger (not three distinguishable events on the transition), the model provides no separate mechanism to distinguish which of the three collision types occurred, which is a precise semantic gap best captured as predicate-null W1 tied to the guard_disjointness contract via the derived reference.
